title: Hosts, Clients, and Servers: MCP's Process Topology

questions.question: A host application needs data from three different MCP servers in one session. How many MCP client instances does the host create to do this?
options: Two clients, since one client can safely serve two servers at once
Three clients, each holding a dedicated connection to one server
One client that opens three separate connections in turn
Zero, because the host process talks to servers directly without a client layer
questions.explanation: The host embeds exactly one client per server connection, so three connected servers require three separate client instances, each bound to exactly one server.

questions.question: A filesystem server launches as a local subprocess over stdio, while a billing server runs on another company's infrastructure and is reached over Streamable HTTP. What follows from that difference?
options: Streamable HTTP servers can only expose resources and prompts, never tools
The stdio server must use OAuth while the HTTP server reads credentials from the environment
The local server crosses a process boundary, the remote one a network boundary
Nothing changes: MCP message shapes stay identical no matter which transport carries them
questions.explanation: Local stdio servers are separate processes on the same machine while remote Streamable HTTP servers cross a network boundary, and a server's trust considerations follow whichever boundary it actually crosses.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches an MCP server primitive with who decides when it is used?
options: Tools are user-controlled, resources are model-controlled, prompts are application-driven
Resources are model-controlled, prompts are application-driven, tools are user-controlled
All three primitives are selected by the server operator before the connection opens
Tools are model-controlled, resources are application-driven, prompts are user-controlled
questions.explanation: The model decides when to call a tool, the host application decides which resources enter context, and the user explicitly selects which prompt to run.

questions.question: A server wants an on-demand language model completion routed through the client's own model access, without embedding a model SDK itself. Which client feature exists for that, and what is its status in 2026-07-28?
options: Sampling, which is deprecated with a migration to LLM provider APIs directly
Elicitation, and it is the current, actively recommended mechanism for this
Logging, and it is deprecated with a migration to stderr or OpenTelemetry
Roots, and it is deprecated with a migration to passing paths as tool arguments
questions.explanation: Sampling lets a server ask the client to run a model completion on its behalf, but it is deprecated in 2026-07-28 and new implementations should call LLM provider APIs directly instead.

questions.question: Two independently written servers both self-report serverInfo.name as "primary" during server/discover, yet a host aggregating both must still route tool calls to the correct one. What does the host key its routing on?
options: The protocol version string that server declares in its capabilities
The connection identifier the host itself assigned when it connected
Whichever server happens to answer the discovery request first
The self-reported serverInfo.name value returned by that server's discover result
questions.explanation: serverInfo is self-reported and never guaranteed unique across independently written servers, so a host must route by the connection identifier it assigned itself, not by a server's own claimed name.

questions.question: A host connects to a files server and a notes server. Both declare a tool literally named search. After the host builds its aggregated registry, how does it expose the second one?
options: It merges both into a single combined search tool that queries both servers at once
It silently overwrites the first entry so only the newest search remains
It keeps the first search as canonical and prefixes the second by server id
It drops the second search tool entirely so the model never sees it
questions.explanation: A collision-safe aggregator keeps the first canonical tool name and exposes a later collision as a server-prefixed name, such as notes/search, so the model can still reach both tools by distinct names.
